purpose: Reference values for matching a typical bright Roblox obby look in the web (three.js) renderer. The same preset is stored in Studio at Workspace/RobloxAssetPack/LightingPreset (inert: move its children into Lighting and copy its attributes to apply).

sky.note: Roblox's current default sky, as found in a fresh Baseplate place (Lighting.Sky). Free images that Roblox ships in its default template; the uploader accounts are DodgerJavi (sky, sun) and meow_pizza (moon), not the Roblox account (see CREDITS.md).
sky.classicSkyAlternative: rbxasset://textures/sky/sky512_{bk,dn,ft,lf,rt,up}.tex (the pre-2020 blue sky that ships inside Studio)

lighting.notes: Roblox's default Baseplate uses Brightness 3, ClockTime 14.5, Ambient and OutdoorAmbient (70,70,70), ColorShift 0. For a brighter obby read on phones, raise OutdoorAmbient to (128,128,128) and add a slightly warm ColorShift_Top. The MCP could not read or set Lighting.Technology (it lacks the RobloxScript capability), so set Future by hand in Studio.

threejsMapping.sun: DirectionalLight, warm white (#fff1d6), intensity ~3 with soft shadows; ClockTime 14 is roughly 55-60 degrees sun elevation
threejsMapping.sky: Use the gradient sky already in web/lib/world.js (zenith #2f7fe6, horizon #bfe4ff) or a cube map made from the skybox IDs above
threejsMapping.ambient: HemisphereLight sky #d9ecff / ground #8a93a6 at ~0.55 approximates OutdoorAmbient 128 + EnvironmentDiffuseScale 1
threejsMapping.neon: Materials with Ke in the pack's MTL files are Roblox Neon: render emissive and let the bloom pass catch them
